newsitem.title: PERU: Lima stocks close higher in thin trading.
newsitem.headline: Lima stocks close higher in thin trading.

text.p: The Lima Stock Exchange closed higher on Monday in thin trade as local investors took positions ahead of Tuesday's market holiday and on expectations of an entry of foreign capital later in the week, brokers said.
The General Index .IGRA rose 0.62 percent to 1,565.5 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index .ISEL gained 0.75 percent to 2,093.3.
Total market volume was a very low 12 million soles ($4.9 million) on 1,082 trades as overall 37 stocks were flat, 26 rose and 21 fell.
"Today was a session which does not deserve any comment," said one broker, who asked not to be named. "Quite simply, nothing happened."
Said Luis Calderon, of Acciones y Valores brokerage: "Some investors bought shares with depressed prices, but they didn't take many risks."
Technical faults at the beginning of the session also hindered trading and affected volume.

Among leaders, the biggest gainers included brewery Backus y Johnston, up 2.64 percent to 2.72 soles on 218,237 shares and food company Consorcio de Alimentos Fabril Pacifico, which gained 1.87 percent to 3.82 soles on 333,718 shares.
Benchmark Telefonica del Peru rose 0.7 percent to 5.77 soles on 700,388 shares.
